newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Swedish April CPI seen rising 0.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Swedish April CPI seen rising 0.2 pct.

text.p: Sweden's consumer price index (CPI) is expected to rise 0.2 percent in April for a year-on-year inflation rate of zero, a Reuters poll of 12 analysts showed on Tuesday.
Forecasts for the monthly figure ranged from 0.2 percent to 0.4 percent, corresponding to a year-on-year rate between a fall of 0.1 percent and a rise of 0.2 percent.
In March, consumer prices rose 0.4 percent for an annualised fall of 0.4 percent, Statistics Sweden previously said.

But later the agency said it had changed its method of calculating the CPI to more accurately take into account household interest costs for the repayment of property loans and revised the March year-on-year figure to zero.
In April 1996, prices rose 0.2 percent and 1.3 percent year-on-year.

Statistics Sweden will publish April consumer prices at 0715 GMT on April 15. It said it would also release revised figures, calculated by the new method, for the period from January 1995 to March 1997 at that time.
Analysts polled who gave a monthly figure were from: Aragon, Carnegie, Consenus, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, HSBC Midland, IDEA, JP Morgan, Penser, S-E-Banken, Swedbank and UBS.

Analysts polled who gave year-on-year figures were from: Carnegie, Consensus, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, HSBC Midland, IDEA, JP Morgan, Penser, PaineWebber, S-E-Banken, Swedbank, Unibank and UBS.
